role.owner.title: The owner's path
role.owner.intro: Set up items and staff, try a full day, then learn to read the figures and close.
role.manager.title: The manager's path
role.manager.intro: Receiving, selling, returns, counting and the day's figures.
role.cashier.title: The cashier's path
role.cashier.intro: Open your shift, sell by scan and by weight, then close after counting the cash.
role.receiver.title: The receiver's path
role.receiver.intro: Receive goods with cost and expiry, and count stock.
role.butcher.title: The butcher's path
role.butcher.intro: Cut meat with balanced weights and make tagines with labels.
role.counter.title: The counter's path
role.counter.intro: Count what you see; the manager approves.
role.accountant.title: The accountant's path
role.accountant.intro: Read the day's figures and pay suppliers.
role.viewer.title: The viewer's path
role.viewer.intro: Read the main screen and the day's figures.
guide.first-look.title: Meet the main screen
guide.first-look.why: From here you see what to do now and where every page is.
guide.first-look.ok: You know where the menu, the next steps and the help button are.
guide.first-look.2: This is the side menu. Each page shows according to your rights.
guide.first-look.3: Your next steps, in order. Example: a cashier sees "open the shift" first.
guide.first-look.4: [[help.this_screen]] explains the page you are on.
guide.first-look.5: Done. You know the screen now.
guide.open-shift.title: Open your shift
guide.open-shift.why: No sale before the shift is open; it records what is in the drawer at the start.
guide.open-shift.ok: [[nav.sell]] opens and the "no shift" message is gone.
guide.open-shift.2: Count the cash in the drawer and type it here. Training example: 500.
guide.open-shift.4: Done. Your shift is open and you move to selling.
guide.open-shift.mistake: If you typed a wrong amount, close the shift with the right count and write why in the note.
guide.first-sale.title: First sale: scan and cash
guide.first-sale.why: The cashier's daily work: scan, pay, receipt.
guide.first-sale.ok: The receipt shows, with the change for the customer.
guide.first-sale.2: Scan the barcode. In training type 6220000000013 and press Enter: mango juice appears.
guide.first-sale.3: Press the plus button so the quantity is 2.
guide.first-sale.5: Type what the customer paid. Example: 100, the total is 70.
guide.first-sale.7: Check the receipt: the change is 30.
guide.first-sale.8: Done. The sale is saved with a receipt number.
guide.first-sale.mistake: If you scanned one too many, press the minus button. The bin deletes the whole line.
guide.weighed-sale.title: Sell by weight
guide.weighed-sale.why: Meat and mince are sold by the kilo; the price comes from the weight.
guide.weighed-sale.ok: The item shows in the cart with its weight and price.
guide.weighed-sale.3: Type part of the name. Example: mince.
guide.weighed-sale.5: Type the weight in kilos. Example: 0,750 or 0.750 means 750 grams.
guide.weighed-sale.6: Check the line in the cart before [[sell.pay]].
guide.weighed-sale.7: Done. The price comes from the weight.
guide.weighed-sale.mistake: If the weight is wrong, delete the line with the bin and add it again.
guide.hold-sale.title: Hold a sale and resume it
guide.hold-sale.why: A customer forgot something: hold the sale and serve the next one.
guide.hold-sale.ok: The sale comes back as it was; prices are checked again.
guide.hold-sale.2: Scan an item. Example: 6220000000020 for rice.
guide.hold-sale.4: Press [[sell.resume]] when the customer is back.
guide.hold-sale.5: Done. At most 10 sales can be on hold.
guide.hold-sale.mistake: If the limit is reached, resume or delete a held sale first.
guide.return-item.title: Return from a receipt
guide.return-item.why: A return comes from its own sale, so money goes back the way it was paid.
guide.return-item.ok: The return amount, the refund method and the reference receipt show.
guide.return-item.2: Type the receipt number. Training example: TR-000001.
guide.return-item.5: Choose the reason. Returned meat always goes to inspection hold.
guide.return-item.7: Done. The return is saved and never deleted.
guide.return-item.mistake: If you refunded too much, delete nothing. Ask the manager for a correcting entry.
guide.close-shift.title: Close your shift
guide.close-shift.why: At the end you count the cash yourself; the program compares after saving.
guide.close-shift.ok: Expected, counted and the difference show.
guide.close-shift.2: Count the cash in the drawer and type it. Example: 570.
guide.close-shift.4: Done. The difference shows only after saving, so the count stays honest.
guide.close-shift.mistake: If there is a difference, write its reason in the note. Do not change the count.
guide.receive-goods.title: Receive goods from a supplier
guide.receive-goods.why: Stock rises only by what really arrived, with its cost and expiry.
guide.receive-goods.ok: A saved message shows, and the item has a new lot in [[nav.stock]].
guide.receive-goods.2: Choose the supplier. In training: the trial supplier.
guide.receive-goods.3: Type the supplier invoice number. Example: F-100.
guide.receive-goods.5: Choose the item. Example: Rice 1 kg.
guide.receive-goods.8: Type the cost of the whole line. Example: 250.
guide.receive-goods.9: Type the expiry date from the pack.
guide.receive-goods.11: Done. 10 packs came in at 25 each.
guide.receive-goods.mistake: If the invoice shows as a duplicate, check it is the rest of the same shipment before confirming.
guide.cut-meat.title: Cut bone-in meat
guide.cut-meat.why: Cutting turns a raw lot into products; the weights must balance.
guide.cut-meat.ok: The new lots show with their weights and expiry dates.
guide.cut-meat.3: Choose the meat lot. In training: Beef bone-in.
guide.cut-meat.4: Type the weight going in, in kilos. Example: 10.
guide.cut-meat.5: Choose the first output. Example: Beef boneless.
guide.cut-meat.7: Press [[add]] for each other output. Example: mince 2, bones 0,5.
guide.cut-meat.8: Type the loss you really measured. Example: 0,5.
guide.cut-meat.9: Check the balance: 10 in, outputs and loss 10.
guide.cut-meat.11: Done. The cost was spread over the outputs.
guide.cut-meat.mistake: Never type a loss you did not measure to balance the weight. Check the weights, and ask the manager if a gap stays.
guide.make-tagine.title: Make tagines with labels
guide.make-tagine.why: A tagine uses meat, marinade and tray once, at preparation.
guide.make-tagine.ok: The pack labels show; each pack has a unique number.
guide.make-tagine.3: Choose the tagine. In training: beef and onion tagine.
guide.make-tagine.4: Type each component. Example: meat 0,8, marinade 0,2 and 2 trays.
guide.make-tagine.5: Type the number of packs. Example: 2.
guide.make-tagine.7: Done. Print the labels and stick them on the packs.
guide.make-tagine.mistake: A tagine never outlives its nearest component. If refused, check the component dates.
guide.count-stock.title: Count a place
guide.count-stock.why: You count what you see without seeing the balance, so the count stays honest.
guide.count-stock.ok: A saved mark shows next to each line you counted.
guide.count-stock.2: Choose the place. Example: display fridge.
guide.count-stock.4: Type what you really count. Example: 2,8 kilo of mince.
guide.count-stock.5: An empty line is not zero. The manager approves after you.
guide.count-stock.6: Done. Your count is saved and waits for approval.
guide.count-stock.mistake: If you typed a wrong number, type the right one in the same line before approval.
guide.day-report.title: Read the day
guide.day-report.why: You see what was sold, what was collected and what needs your decision.
guide.day-report.ok: You know the difference between net sales and cash collected.
guide.day-report.3: Read sales, returns and net sales.
guide.day-report.4: Net sales are not cash: they include credit and transfers waiting for confirmation.
guide.day-report.5: Done. Details are under each number.
guide.close-day.title: Close the day
guide.close-day.why: After closing, the day's figures are kept, and each later correction is listed under it.
guide.close-day.ok: "Closed" shows, with later corrections below it.
guide.close-day.1: Open [[nav.reports]] after every shift is closed.
guide.close-day.3: Done. Nothing can be posted on this date any more.
guide.close-day.mistake: Never change the computer clock to post on a closed day. Post the correction today.
guide.add-product.title: Add a new item
guide.add-product.why: An item needs a code, a name, a price and a barcode before it is sold.
guide.add-product.ok: The item shows in the list with its price.
guide.add-product.4: Type the name. Example: Sugar 1 kg.
guide.add-product.6: Scan the pack barcode into its field.
guide.add-product.8: Done. The item is ready to receive and sell.
guide.add-product.mistake: A barcode of another item is refused. Two items are never merged automatically.
guide.pay-supplier.title: Pay a supplier
guide.pay-supplier.why: A payment lowers what you owe the supplier, from the safe or the drawer.
guide.pay-supplier.ok: The balance owed goes down in the supplier statement.
guide.pay-supplier.2: Press the supplier's name. In training: the trial supplier.
guide.pay-supplier.5: Done. The payment is in the supplier statement.
guide.pay-supplier.mistake: If you paid a wrong amount, delete nothing. Record the correction as a new entry.
guide.add-user.title: Add an employee
guide.add-user.why: Each person signs in with their own name, so the program knows who did what.
guide.add-user.ok: The employee shows in the list as "must change password".
guide.add-user.2: Type the sign-in name. Example: ahmed.
guide.add-user.3: Type a temporary password of at least 8 characters.
guide.add-user.6: Done. The employee changes the password at first sign-in.
guide.add-user.mistake: When an employee leaves, press [[set.stop_user]]. No account is ever deleted.
guide.backup-now.title: Take a backup
guide.backup-now.why: A backup protects the shop's data if the computer breaks.
guide.backup-now.3: Copy the backup to a flash drive or another computer every week.
guide.backup-now.4: Done. The program also takes a daily backup by itself.
guide.change-password.title: Change your password
guide.change-password.why: Your password is yours alone. Changing it signs out any other device using your account.
guide.change-password.ok: A changed message shows and you carry on.
guide.change-password.1: Press the key button under the menu.
guide.change-password.3: Type a new password twice, at least 8 characters.
guide.change-password.5: Done. In training, keep the password so colleagues can sign in.
guide.lock-screen.title: Lock the screen
guide.lock-screen.why: You step away without anyone selling in your name.
guide.lock-screen.ok: The lock screen shows and opens only with your password.
guide.lock-screen.1: Press the lock button under the menu.
guide.lock-screen.2: To come back, type your password. For a colleague press [[lock.switch]].
guide.lock-screen.3: Done. Your unpaid cart stays saved under your name.
problem.sign-in.see: You cannot sign in, the screen is locked, or a new password is asked for.
problem.sign-in.why: Wrong password, too many tries, or the owner typed a temporary password.
problem.sign-in.do.1: Type the sign-in name and password carefully.
problem.sign-in.do.2: If asked for a new password, choose one of at least 8 characters.
problem.sign-in.still: Ask the owner for a new temporary password.
problem.staff-accounts.see: Adding or stopping an employee is refused.
problem.staff-accounts.why: The name is taken, you are stopping yourself, or this is the last owner.
problem.staff-accounts.do.2: To stop an owner, add another owner first.
problem.staff-accounts.still: If you forgot your password, run owner-recovery.bat on the shop computer.
problem.needs-approval.see: A manager approval is asked for, or the action is not in your rights.
problem.needs-approval.why: The action is beyond your rights, like a large discount or a meat return.
problem.needs-approval.do.1: Ask the manager to type their name and password in the approval window.
problem.needs-approval.do.2: Hiding a button is not enough; the server always checks rights.
problem.needs-approval.still: Ask the owner about your role's rights.
problem.shift-and-drawer.see: Selling or paying out is refused because of the shift or the drawer.
problem.shift-and-drawer.why: No open shift, or the drawer cash is not enough to refund or pay.
problem.shift-and-drawer.do.2: If cash is short, ask the manager for a deposit into the drawer.
problem.shift-and-drawer.still: Check the expected drawer amount with the manager.
problem.scanning.see: The scan shows a wrong code, Arabic letters, or nothing.
problem.scanning.why: The label is damaged, the keyboard language is Arabic, or the scanner belongs to another window.
problem.scanning.do.1: Scan the label again, or type the number printed under it.
problem.scanning.do.2: Open [[nav.scanner]] and try the test sheet.
problem.scanning.still: Ask the manager to set the scanner up for this computer.
problem.sale-price.see: The price changed at payment, the item has no price, or it is not for sale.
problem.sale-price.why: The manager changed the price after the scan, or it is an internal component.
problem.sale-price.do.1: Check the new total with the customer before confirming.
problem.sale-price.do.2: If the item has no price, ask the manager to set it.
problem.sale-price.still: No sale was saved; try again after fixing it.
problem.stock-for-sale.see: The sale is refused: not enough stock, or the lot is expired, held or recalled.
problem.stock-for-sale.why: The program never sells expired, held or recalled goods.
problem.stock-for-sale.do.1: Do not sell the piece. Put it aside and tell the manager.
problem.stock-for-sale.do.2: The manager checks the lot in [[nav.stock]].
problem.stock-for-sale.still: Do not change the quantity to push the sale through.
problem.labelled-packs.see: The pack label is refused, or says it was sold before.
problem.labelled-packs.why: Each pack has a unique number sold only once.
problem.labelled-packs.do.1: Check whether the same pack was scanned twice.
problem.labelled-packs.do.2: If the pack is damaged, write it off in [[nav.stock]].
problem.labelled-packs.still: Ask the butcher to reprint the label without a new number.
problem.payments.see: Payment is refused, a transfer waits for confirmation, or the customer is over the limit.
problem.payments.why: A customer message is not proof; a transfer counts once confirmed.
problem.payments.do.1: Type the transfer or card reference.
problem.payments.do.2: For credit, choose the customer and check the credit limit.
problem.payments.still: Ask the manager to confirm or reject the transfer.
problem.returns.see: The return is refused or the amount is lower than expected.
problem.returns.why: You never refund more than was sold or paid by each method.
problem.returns.do.1: Check the receipt number and the quantity.
problem.returns.do.2: Choose refund by the original method.
problem.returns.still: With a buy-and-get offer, returning the free piece refunds nothing.
problem.customer-accounts.see: The customer account waits for review and no cash is refunded.
problem.customer-accounts.why: After upgrading old data, a collection could not be tied to an invoice.
problem.customer-accounts.do.2: The owner ties the collection to its invoice.
problem.customer-accounts.still: Do not change amounts by hand.
problem.receiving.why: Missing expiry, a duplicate invoice, or more than the registered invoice.
problem.receiving.do.1: Type the expiry from the pack.
problem.receiving.do.2: If the invoice is a duplicate, check it is the rest of the shipment.
problem.receiving.still: Goods without a date are held, not sold.
problem.suppliers.why: The receipt belongs to another supplier, or the supplier note number is already used.
problem.suppliers.do.1: Choose the right supplier and receipt.
problem.suppliers.do.2: Use a unique reference for every credit note. If old cost weights cannot be proved, ask the accountant to review the original operation; never guess. Finally settled claims accept no new credit note.
problem.cutting.see: Cutting is refused: weights do not balance or the expiry is wrong.
problem.cutting.why: Input weight must equal output plus measured losses, and cutting requires valid raw-meat inputs and outputs.
problem.cutting.do.2: Never type a loss you did not measure to balance the weight.
problem.cutting.still: If a gap stays, tell the manager before approving.
problem.recipes.see: Preparing from the recipe is refused.
problem.recipes.why: A missing component, an unapproved substitute, or more meat than there is.
problem.recipes.do.1: Use the components written in the recipe.
problem.recipes.do.2: A substitute must be approved in the recipe itself.
problem.recipes.still: Ask the owner to review the recipe in [[nav.catalog]].
problem.freezer-and-places.see: Moving from or into the freezer is refused.
problem.freezer-and-places.why: Thaw frozen stock into a fridge. Thawed goods and their outputs must remain in allowed cold storage, never an ordinary shelf or a freezer.
problem.freezer-and-places.do.2: Choose a prep fridge or a display fridge.
problem.freezer-and-places.still: The owner sets the thawed period in settings.
problem.recalls.see: A recall or release does not change.
problem.recalls.why: A recall is lifted once by a written decision; then lots are checked one by one.
problem.recalls.do.2: Write the reason for the decision clearly.
problem.recalls.still: Do not release a lot before checking it.
problem.counting.see: A count does not start or a number is refused.
problem.counting.why: A count is already open for this place, or it was closed.
problem.counting.do.1: Continue the open count from the list.
problem.counting.do.2: If the count was closed, start a new one.
problem.items.see: Adding an item or an offer is refused.
problem.items.why: The code or barcode is used, or another offer covers the same period.
problem.items.do.2: Never merge two items under one barcode.
problem.items.still: End the current offer before adding a new one.
problem.closed-days.see: The action is refused because the day is closed, or the date is wrong.
problem.closed-days.why: After a day is closed nothing is posted on its date.
problem.closed-days.do.1: Post the correction on today's date.
problem.closed-days.do.2: Check the computer clock; never change it to get around the close.
problem.closed-days.still: The correction shows under the closed day.
problem.backup-restore.see: A backup or a restore does not work.
problem.backup-restore.why: The backup is damaged or from another program, or the folder is not empty.
problem.backup-restore.do.1: Try a newer backup from the flash drive.
problem.backup-restore.do.2: A restore always goes into a new empty folder.
problem.backup-restore.still: Call technical support with the backup.
problem.settings-values.why: The value is outside the allowed range.
problem.settings-values.do.1: Type a number within the range shown under the field.
problem.settings-values.do.2: Leave the field empty if no value is approved yet.
problem.settings-values.still: Ask technical support about the range.
problem.typing.why: A field is empty or has a number that cannot be read.
problem.typing.do.1: Type the number with one decimal mark. Example: 12,50 or 12.50.
problem.typing.do.2: Write the reason in its field clearly.
problem.typing.still: Nothing was saved; fix the field and try again.
